name: Cache and temporary storage eviction
plain: The system may delete cache and temporary files when storage runs low; other files stay.
meaning: Apps cannot rely on cache data staying. Android clears cache dirs and reports a cache quota; iOS purges Caches and tmp when space is needed, and flags files as purgeable.

android.persistence: Cache cleared on low storage or by the user; per app cache quota via StorageManager
android.note: Low storage clears oldest cache first; quota set by the system

ios.persistence: Caches and tmp purged by the system when low; Documents is not
ios.note: Purge happens while the app is not running; Documents and Application Support are kept

limits.headline: Can store temporary files that the system may delete when your storage runs low
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app saves cache files while you use it
can: Save cache and temporary files, such as image thumbnails
Keep them until storage runs low or you clear them
Rebuild them after the system deletes them
cannot: Keep cache forever; Android clears oldest cache first when space is low
Count on cache staying while iPhone is low on storage; it is purged when the app is not running
Lose Documents or Application Support files on iPhone from this purge
Stop you from using Settings, then Storage, then Clear cache on Android
limits.differs: Android sets a cache quota and clears oldest first. iPhone purges the caches folder while the app is not running.

story.what_it_is: The phone may delete an app's cache and temporary files when it runs low on space.
story.for_you: When your storage is nearly full, the phone may quietly wipe cached images and temporary files. You may see an app reload things it had already downloaded. Your saved files stay.
story.for_makers: Makers must treat caches as disposable and rebuild them when they vanish. It lets the phone free space without asking you, and makers should not hide needed files in caches.

use_cases.example: A streaming app loses its cached thumbnails when space is low and downloads them again.
A photo feed app reloads old images after the phone cleared its cache.
A map app re downloads map tiles it used to have stored in cache.
A game re downloads optional textures but keeps your saved game files safe.
A music app keeps your downloads in permanent storage so they are not wiped, but cached previews may go.
A developer tests low storage to see if the app copes with missing cache.

story.android_note: Android clears cache folders and reports a cache quota for each app.
story.ios_note: iOS purges Caches and tmp folders when space is needed and flags files as purgeable.

legit_uses: Offline content that can be rebuilt

history.change: System purges Caches when space is needed
